source_row.rationale: A dual relationship occurs when a nurse has both a professional and a pre-existing personal relationship (such as friendship or family) with a client, which requires careful, thoughtful attention to maintaining appropriate professional boundaries and objectivity, and in some cases may warrant discussion with a supervisor about the most appropriate way to proceed.
source_row.source_detail: 2024 guidance on professional nurse-client boundaries and boundary crossings/violations; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: NCSBN — A Nurse's Guide to Professional Boundaries
source_row.stem: A nurse is caring for a client who also happens to be a personal friend outside of work, and the nurse initially assumes this pre-existing friendship poses no real professional complication as long as care is provided competently. This situation illustrates the concept of:
